concepts.name: Multilingual jailbreaking
concepts.summary: A prompt-side attack in which a request that an aligned model refuses in English is answered when the same request is posed in another language.
concepts.explanation: Deng et al. (2023) report that a model's refusal behaviour does not transfer evenly across the languages it can read, so translating a harmful request can get it answered. The paper lists this alongside many-shot jailbreaking as an example of the prompt-based branch of the jailbreak literature: the attacker changes only the input, and the weights are untouched. That is what separates it from the finetuning attacks the paper's own jailbroken control belongs to, where the attacker changes the model. The citation is a one-line pointer in Section 5 - the paper runs no multilingual evaluations of its own and makes no claim about whether the insecure model behaves this way.

citedFrom.refText: Deng, Y., Zhang, W., Pan, S. J., and Bing, L. Multilingual jailbreak challenges in large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.06474, 2023.
citedFrom.whyNeeded: The paper names the attack in a citation list without describing it; what a multilingual jailbreak is lives entirely in the cited paper.
